findings.exploitation: A non-standard SUID executable runs with root privileges. If it contains logic flaws, shell escapes, or relative library loads, a local user may escalate privileges.
findings.mitigation: Remove the SUID bit if not required: chmod u-s /opt/privesc-lab/find_suid
findings.title: Non-standard SUID binary found

findings.exploitation: The executable has documented command execution or shell breakout capabilities when invoked with elevated privileges.
findings.mitigation: Review GTFOBins documentation for find and remove SUID bit or restrict execution permissions.
findings.title: SUID binary with known GTFOBins bypass found

findings.exploitation: Any local account can alter this configuration file, potentially redirecting application flow, injecting arguments, or tampering with parameters read by root.
findings.mitigation: Restrict write permissions to root or authorized group: chmod o-w /opt/privesc-lab/world_writable.conf
findings.title: World-writable configuration file

findings.exploitation: Users can create, replace, or delete files owned by other users within this directory. If a privileged service relies on this directory, symlink or race attacks may occur.
findings.mitigation: Apply the sticky bit (chmod +t) or remove world-write permissions (chmod o-w).
findings.title: World-writable directory without sticky bit

findings.exploitation: The specified user can run privileged commands without supplying a password. If broad or unconstrained, this allows immediate privilege boundary transitions.
findings.mitigation: Require password authentication and scope sudo permissions to specific commands and parameters.
findings.title: Sudo NOPASSWD grant detected

findings.exploitation: A script executed periodically by root is writable by an unprivileged user. Any commands appended to the script will run with full root privileges on the next schedule.
findings.mitigation: Change ownership of the script to root:root and set permissions to 0755 or 0700.
findings.title: Root cron job executes user-writable script

findings.exploitation: The system service runs as root but executes a script owned or writable by an unprivileged account. Modifying the script gives root code execution upon service activation.
findings.mitigation: Set root ownership on the service script and restrict file write permissions.
findings.title: Systemd service unit executes writable script as root

findings.exploitation: The capability cap_setuid allows the process to arbitrarily change its UID to 0 (root). If attached to an interpreter or utility, full root escalation is trivial.
findings.title: Binary with elevated Linux capabilities found

findings.exploitation: Local privilege escalation flaw in the Linux kernel (Dirty Pipe). Notice: Distribution kernels may contain backported fixes; verify against distribution vendor errata.
findings.mitigation: Update kernel packages via apt/dnf and reboot into the latest security release.
findings.title: Running kernel version matches known advisory range (Advisory)
